method.score: coverage(max cosine to a DEV query) + lambda * (1 - redundancy(mean cosine to k-NN))
method.retrieval: RRF(k=60) over BM25 + dense top-100, no cross-encoder (identical for all three arms)
method.eval: NDCG@10 on held-out ESCI test queries; the test split is never used for selection
method.cost_model: measured index build time + embedding time extrapolated from a measured encode rate, priced at $0.0017/CPU-minute

note: Dropping catalogue rows removes relevant documents, so some NDCG loss is arithmetically unavoidable. The honest question is how the selected subset compares with a random subset of the SAME size, which is why the random arm is reported alongside, together with each arm's relevant_doc_retention.
interpretation: In ESCI every graded label is bound to one product_id, so a dropped relevant document cannot be substituted by a near-twin and NDCG under index pruning tracks relevant_doc_retention almost mechanically. Uniform random pruning retains exactly keep_frac of EVERY query's relevant set; a model-based scorer can only beat it by predicting which documents will be judged relevant for unseen queries. Compare the arms' relevant_doc_retention against keep_frac=0.4 to see how much signal each strategy actually carries.
